title: CyrusOne and KEP top out 48MW data center in Osaka, Japan
html:
CyrusOne and Kansai Electric Power Company (KEP) have topped out a data center in Osaka, Japan.

The company this week announced that the first CyrusOne KEP data center in Japan has topped out its steel structure.

The OSK1 facility in Kansai is set to offer 48MW of IT capacity across 11,560 sqm (124,430 sq ft). Ground was broken on the site in September 2024, and the first phase will be operational by Q1 2028.

“We are delighted to celebrate today’s topping out,” said CyrusOne KEP co-CEO, Takashi Mishima.

The milestone was marked with a traditional Japanese Jōtōshiki (topping-out ceremony), celebrating the completion of the building’s main structural frame and wishing for the safety and successful completion of the remaining construction work. The ceremony features gold and silver bolts driven into the final steel beam.

CyrusOne and KEPCO announced a 50:50 joint venture to develop new data centers across Japan in May 2023. The two companies plan to invest at least one trillion yen ($7 billion) over the next decade and reach a business scale of 900MW (600MW IT capacity). Further project plans haven't been shared, but the company has previously said it aims to develop in Tokyo and other major markets across Japan

Founded in 1951, KEPCO owns and operates dozens of energy generation plants totaling more than 35GW of capacity. The company owns ISP Optage Inc., which in 2023 announced plans to build a new data center in Osaka, as well as real estate development firm Kanden.

KKR-owned CyrusOne operates or is developing more than 40 data centers across the US and Europe, but this is the company's first expansion into Asia.
summary: First facility under the pair's Japanese joint venture
